purpose: Teach: 神経質/奪い/無駄遣い/辛口/刃物/利い/ろくに/使い道

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: 若い頃、私、神経質なところ、結構、あったんだぞ、ばあさん、覚えてる?本当に、お前に、迷惑かけた、絶対。
lines.en: When I was young, I was quite a nervous person, you remember? I really put you through a lot, absolutely.
lines.style: Soft opening, looking back with gentle regret. Slow, measured pace. Seeks her confirmation quietly—not performing grief, just turning over old memories. Voice trails slightly on 'absolutely,' as if still absorbing how much time has passed.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: うん。若い頃、二人の時間、奪い合う仕事、忙しかったわよね、あなた、覚えてる?本当に、頑張ったわよね、本気で。
lines.en: Yes. When we were young, work stole our time together, you were so busy. You remember? You really did your best, truly.
lines.style: Nodding along with his memory, but her voice carries warmth underneath. Not sad—just remembering. Gentle affirmation in the middle, then a small strengthening on 'truly,' as if to say his effort mattered and she saw it.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: 無駄遣い、若い頃、私たち、本気で、しないように、頑張ってきたよな、ばあさん、本当に、賢明、絶対。
lines.en: We really made an effort not to waste those young years, didn't we? You were absolutely wise about it, gran.
lines.style: Quieter now, more internal. A thoughtful pause before speaking. Steady tone—not cheerful, but solid. The words come as something he's thought about many times. Slight breath before 'absolutely,' grounding the appreciation.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: 昔のお祖父ちゃん、辛口の評論家でしたわよね、覚えてる、あなた?本気で、厳しい人だった、絶対、本気。
lines.en: Your grandfather back then—he was quite a sharp critic, wasn't he? Do you remember? He was stern, truly harsh.
lines.style: Her voice softens into the memory, a little wry affection creeping in. Not complaint, more like—'remember how he was?' Slight emphasis on the description of him, then a small fade, as if seeing his face.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: 昔、刃物、本気で、研ぐ、お祖母ちゃん、上手だったよな、ばあさん、覚えてる?本当に、職人技、絶対。
lines.en: I remember your grandmother was wonderful at sharpening blades. That skillful hand she had—you remember? True craftsmanship, absolutely.
lines.style: Warmth in the voice now, genuine admiration. Opens gently, then lets the image unfold. Almost reverent on 'craftsmanship'—not just skill, but care. The 'absolutely' lands with quiet pride, not force.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: お祖父ちゃんの、ピリッと利いた、説教、本気で、家族、覚えてるわよね、あなた、本当に、感謝、絶対、本気。
lines.en: Your grandfather's sharp words stung, but the family felt them. You remember? I'm grateful for him—truly, I really am.
lines.style: Thoughtful, almost vulnerable. She's connecting the dots: his harshness meant something. Voice carries both the sting and the acceptance. Slight breath before 'truly'—this is sincere, not performed. Warm closing.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: 最近、ろくに、外出、できなくなってきたわよな、ばあさん、お互いに、家で、ゆっくり、過ごそうね、絶対、本気。
lines.en: Lately we can't get out much anymore, can we? Let's just spend quiet time at home together, you and me. Truly.
lines.style: Gentle statement of fact, but not resigned. Opens with acceptance, then shifts into something almost tender—an invitation. Slower pace. The 'truly' is a quiet promise, not demand. Voice settles at the end.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: 年金の使い道、本気で、考えて、計画的に、使いましょうね、あなた、絶対、本当に、感謝、しないとね、本気。
lines.en: We should think carefully about how we spend our pension and plan it out together, dear. We really need to be grateful for what we have.
lines.style: Warm, practical tone—not bossy but clear. She's thinking aloud, and it includes him. Slight lift on the planning part, then a softening at the close. The gratitude isn't abstract; it's grounded. Closes with quiet sincerity.
